record.file_problem: none; the full technical report is present.
record.tranche_reason: The report mentions scaling laws as background but does not test or rely on them. Its own loss result is a training-loss response to batch-size changes in one model, not a test of the listed scaling-law versions.
record.gate_note: The report cites Hoffmann et al. for updated scaling laws. Figure 2 and §2.3 report training cross-entropy during one Falcon2-11B run and abrupt loss drops after batch-size doublings. These are not held-out losses or a sweep over model size, data, or compute. The benchmark evaluations are checkpoint scores, not tests of downstream predictability from scaling laws.
record.test_reason: The Falcon2-11B technical report cites Hoffmann et al. only as background for training on more data. Its loss curve is training cross-entropy for one 11B run, showing drops after batch-size doublings. It has no sweep over parameters, data or compute, no held-out loss fit, no extrapolation and no allocation study. The checkpoint benchmark scores (Table 5) are reported against tokens for one model, with no scaling or loss-based prediction tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also present Falcon2-11B as matching or beating similar-size open models on benchmarks. They do say batch-size doublings presumably reduced spike frequency, and that spikes fell as the learning rate decayed. They draw no conclusion on scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The report does not apply a scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation method.
record.method_sensitivity: Training loss changed abruptly following batch-size doublings; spike frequency was reported to decrease as learning rate decayed.

fits_no_version.finding: In the Falcon2-11B stage-1 run, each batch-size doubling (2K to 32K samples) was followed by an abrupt drop in training loss. The authors attribute this to reduced optimisation noise, as with learning-rate decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing batch size mid-training produces an abrupt drop in training loss, analogous to learning-rate decay.

record.problems: The loss observation is for training loss, not held-out loss, and comes from a single model run; the drops are shown in a figure without separately stated numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: No held-out scaling sweep, compute-optimal allocation results, architecture-controlled comparisons, or scaling-law predictions are reported. Downstream benchmark checkpoint scores are not extracted as scaling-law evidence because the report does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: No held-out loss across parameters, tokens or compute; only a single-run training-loss curve.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters versus tokens.
Head dimension 128 versus 64 is said to give a 'slight boost' at unreported 3B scale, with no numbers. No controlled shape sweep.
The VLM is fine-tuned and benchmarked with no scaling fit; no other regimes are fitted.
Benchmarks are reported at checkpoints of one model; predictability from scale or loss is not tested.
No comparison of fits or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: Reader's relation and tranche are confirmed. Rows r2–r4 split a single textual statement into per-step rows; they could be merged into one row.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out loss power laws across parameters, tokens, or compute and several orders of magnitude.
No small-run fits or predictions for larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No scaling-law tests across other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream benchmarks are reported at checkpoints, but the report does not test whether their performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law fits, exponents, or fitting choices.
